headline: Quantum Mechanics, Without the Mystique
lede: This patient introduction builds quantum mechanics from classical physics through uncertainty, superposition, tunneling, and competing interpretations. Its formulas, glossary, and references favor conceptual clarity over easy intuition.

headline: OBS Studio Rebuilds Its Plugin Pipeline
lede: OBS 33 updates Chromium, changes plugin loading, and adds capture, audio, and Arm64 improvements. Migrate before OBS 34: legacy plugin locations are living on borrowed time.

headline: Kimi Unveils a Million-Token Open Model
lede: Kimi K3.1 Pro pairs a three-trillion-parameter-class design with a one-million-token context window; Highspeed targets two- to three-times faster responses. Full weights are promised, positioning the release against the proprietary frontier.

headline: The iPhone Attack Chain Reaches Persistence
lede: Researchers demonstrate one-click compromises involving Signal and iMessage, along with access that can survive a reboot. The technical details are still forthcoming; the warning is already concrete.

headline: A Positron Spends a Month in Captivity
lede: An electromagnetic trap holds a single positron for at least a month without physical walls. The technique gives physicists a quieter view of quantum states, magnetic moments, and matter’s cosmic imbalance.

headline: Distributed SQLite Is a Decade of Tradeoffs
lede: Twelve years of projects have turned SQLite replication into a family of choices, from Raft consensus to WAL streaming and eventual consistency. The history is less a victory lap than a map of operational compromises.
pullquote: Distributed SQLite is not one technology; it is a negotiation between control, consistency, and recovery.

headline: Pure Functional Code Closes on C
lede: Roc’s DEFLATE compressor comes within 8.9 percent of libdeflate on one AMD system and 2.6 percent on an M1. The benchmark is narrow, but its safety and purity guarantees make the result worth measuring.

headline: Banking Apps Make Room for GrapheneOS
lede: Roughly a dozen banking apps now explicitly permit GrapheneOS, even as about 10 percent still block non-Google-approved systems. Privacy gains meet the quiet friction of compatibility checks, compliance, and account switching.

headline: Apple Turns a 404 Into an iPod
lede: A nonexistent Apple Music URL opens onto a lovingly recreated click-wheel interface instead of a bare error. Beneath the nostalgia, the page still performs its modern duty: inviting visitors into an $11.99 monthly subscription.

headline: SimCity Makes a 16 MHz Chip Feel Larger
lede: The original city builder spread its simulation across 16 frames, updating traffic, fire, crime, and taxation on staggered schedules. On a 16 MHz 386SX, tolerating small delays became the essential optimization.
